cross_language_consistency_note: 1. One harness, one profile, ten languages. Every language's offline check was run by the same script (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-koba-Desktop-Quidra/c7dc7758-3bc7-4b38-ac54-4af31eae0682/scratchpad/depsimp/offline_run.py) over the same 11-workload E7 set (mb01..mb11), with the same sandbox profile denying IP networking and the same freshly created empty HOME/cache tree, and each language used its own frozen_toolchain_recipes build and run command and nothing else. A control curl under the identical profile failed (exit 7) while the same curl outside it returned HTTP 200, so 'network disabled' means the same thing for all ten. 2. D_total was proved, not assumed, and by each language's own mechanism: quidra package lock for Quidra, --emit=dep-info for Rust, jdeps for Java and Kotlin, go list std for Go, sys.stdlib_module_names for Python, clang++ -H for C++, otool -L for Swift, the @import census for Zig, and an ancestor node_modules scan plus the in-source `declare` census for TypeScript. All ten came out 0. 3. The only thing separating the two levels awarded is install_units, read off the install_units_table that the rubric froze on 2026-09-17 before scoring; no scorer judgement entered that value for any language. The eight languages at 1 all got 100 and the two at 2 both got 80, with no other input able to move them, exactly as the rubric's exhaustiveness_verification states ('pinning and install_units are irrelevant at D_total = 0 except for the 100-vs-80 step'). 4. Where the same observable evidence existed, the same level was awarded regardless of how flattering it was: C++, Java and Kotlin have NO first-party pinning mechanism and Quidra, Rust, Go, Swift, Zig, Python and TypeScript do, yet pinning moved no language's level, so C++ and Java tie Rust and Go at 100 and Kotlin ties TypeScript at 80. Symmetrically, rustc and quidra were both found to require an external system C toolchain at COMPILE time (rustc: "error: linker `cc` not found"; quidra: "Clang++ 15 or newer is required for native code generation"), and neither was re-counted, because the frozen counting rule keys install_units on a runtime or SDK needed to EXECUTE the corpus, and both produce self-contained executables. Applying a compile-side reading instead would move Rust and Quidra together from 100 to 80 and change nothing else; that counterfactual is disclosed so the sensitivity is visible, and the frozen table is what was applied. 5. Evidence order: Quidra was collected LAST, per global_rules.evidence_collection_order.
limitations: E7 IS INCOMPLETE FOR ALL TEN LANGUAGES. The rubric defines D_total over 'the complete frozen Standard workload corpus'. Only the 11 micro-benchmark programs exist; the SVM, GMM and LightGrad implementations are recorded as Not Executed (0 of 60) in benchmark/2026-09-17-7677581/NOT_EXECUTED.md section 5. The measurement therefore covers the micro corpus only - identically for all ten languages, so the comparison is fair, but D_total is a lower bound on the full corpus. Spec section 7's bar on outsourcing the core computation to external libraries means the missing workloads were required to be standard-library-only too, which is why the rubric itself predicts D_total = 0; that prediction is unverified for 3 of 4 workload families, for every language.

TWO DELIBERATE, DISCLOSED DEVIATIONS FROM THE FROZEN RECIPE CELLS, APPLIED IDENTICALLY TO ALL TEN LANGUAGES. (a) Network disable: the host's network settings were not changed; each build and run command ran under a per-process sandbox-exec profile denying IP network-outbound/inbound/bind, with an in-run control proving the denial. (b) Cache clear: the per-language `rm -rf` cells were not executed against the operator's real caches (~/Library/Caches/pip 1.6G, ~/.cache/zig 1.3G, ~/.npm 667M of the machine owner's re-downloadable data). Instead HOME and every documented per-tool cache variable were redirected into a freshly created empty tree, which is a strictly stronger 'cache emptied' condition. The cache paths named by the frozen cells that did not exist on this host at all (~/.cargo/registry, ~/.cargo/git, ~/.m2/repository, ~/.gradle/caches, ~/.konan, ~/.cache/pip, ~/Library/Caches/zig) already satisfied their cells with no action. Neither deviation can favour or disfavour any single language, since both were applied uniformly.

EVIDENCE-CUTOFF CORROBORATION IS ASYMMETRIC, AND IN QUIDRA'S DISFAVOUR ONLY IN THE SENSE THAT QUIDRA'S IS THE STRONGER. Quidra's E2 was pinned to the v0.2.0 git tag, published 2026-09-17T09:36:30Z (verified through the GitHub releases API) and byte-identical to the local checkout by SHA-256; Quidra v0.3.0, published 2026-09-18, was excluded as post-cutoff. The nine non-Quidra E2 pages were fetched live on 2026-09-18 and archive.org corroboration that the quoted sentence existed on or before 2026-09-17 could NOT be obtained - the Wayback availability API returned HTTP 429 (rate limited) for all six URLs tried. Those nine E2 citations support the `pinning` quantity only, which changes no language's level at D_total = 0, so no score depends on them.

pinning for C++, Java and Kotlin is recorded as NOT AVAILABLE under a strict reading of first_party_definition (the tool_admissibility_test that admits Maven, Gradle, CMake and npm elsewhere in the rubric explicitly does not extend to the DEP indicators). Under the wider reading those three would have pinning = available. The reading is disclosed because it is genuinely arguable; it changes no score in this metric, because pinning is inert at D_total = 0.

SIDE EFFECT ON THE OPERATOR'S FILESYSTEM: `quidra package lock` writes quidra.lock into the command's working directory. An early evidence command was run from /Users/koba/Desktop/Quidra and created /Users/koba/Desktop/Quidra/quidra.lock (15 bytes, content 'quidra-lock-v1', no entries). Removing it was refused by this session's permission policy, so it is still there and can be deleted safely. All later lock runs were confined to the scratch directory.

Level 100 has no ceiling above it, so genuinely different degrees of self-containment collapse: Zig needed no external toolchain at all, C++ and Swift are part of the Apple toolchain that Rust and Quidra shell out to, and all five score 100. The rubric has no instrument to separate them and none was invented.
